prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

U0046: However, current xEVAS vendors are not required to imple- ment an AR form factor as the necessary display for their spacesuits, which is the hypothesized ideal solution for future operations.
U0047: EXP-EVA-0042 and subsequently this document continues to hypothesize that an augmented reality experience for the crew member will yield the most desired crew informatics interface possible to conduct an EVA.
U0048: See Section 3.2 for more discussion on the value proposition of an augmented reality system.
U0049: In summary, there exists a variety of higher level descriptions of how future EVA operations might be performed.
U0050: However, these existing concept of operations descriptions do not provide the amount Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 15 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations Figure 3.1: Phases of Operations for the xEVA System as defined in Section 4.1.3 of EXP- EVA-0042.
U0051: Figure 3.2: Annotated example from EXP-0042 Figure 5.2 that highlights how an AR Device must be integrated with the surrounding assets that encompass the broader EVA system which includes electronic systems and other human agents upon which the suited crew members must dependent to perform EVA work. of detail required to actually situate how an advanced informatics system might support future user work demands during an EVA.
U0052: The contents found in Section 5 below focus on expanding Phase 7 Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 16 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations Figure 3.3: Summary of desired features and vendor requirements for an advanced infor- matics display for EVA operations.
U0053: "EVA Operations" via a series of use-cases. 3.2 Value Proposition for Augmented Reality This document does not attempt to document all possible informatics display form factors and their corresponding value propositions.
U0054: Both the narratives and user interface solutions in this document are directly applicable to a multitude of display form factors.
U0055: However, we make a deliberate attempt to propose that an augmented reality system as an informatics display technology offers the most desired end result of capabilities to support future EVA operations.
U0056: The value proposition discussed in this section that motivates the Joint AR solution [11] was driven by the design philosophies outlined below: An advanced informatics display and control system for suited crew operations should: • Maximize EV crew productivity without compromising their safety. • Minimize the number of discrete physical acts required by the EV crew to operate. • Minimize the amount of time required to change from the current state to a desired state. • Minimize the interference with other means of communication among the work system (e.g., audio, visual). • Provide redundant means of control for EV crew.
U0057: Simply put, EVA is the most expensive, demanding, and arguably the riskiest phase of human spaceflight.
U0058: Crew time during EVA is precious and any time spent not achieving EVA goals is time wasted.
U0059: AR as technology theoretically offers the fastest mode of information access by simply having the data immediately in view and contextualized within crew surroundings for consumption.
U0060: In other words, crew would not be required to physically handle a piece of separate display hard- ware like a portable display (e.g. tablet) which requires time and attention of the crew member.
U0061: Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 17 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations Additionally, AR that is integrated with the helmet bubble offers the potential to align digital content within the real-world view from the crew member’s first person perspective.
U0062: This capability is known as registered AR and could further reduce the necessary time for the crew member to view and understand digital content while performing EVA.
U0063: For example, the crew could simply see the desti- nation they need to reach in their real-world by looking at the horizon without ever having to look at a 2-dimensional map and perform the orienting work required to transform 2-D map data into their 3-D surroundings to identify where to travel.
U0064: In addition to the display form factor, numerous different control schemes should be considered for feasibility, ease of use, and overall functionality compatible with a suit-compatible AR system.
U0065: The Joint AR advocates that a multi-modal control scheme that includes both direct EV control (e.g. physical crew control and hands free control), in tandem with remote control offers the most flexibil- ity to support EVA work dynamics.
U0066: EVA work ebbs and flows through a series of possible situations that necessitate a fluid control scheme among the broader flight team.
